issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that each point x+y of Ω+Ω equals 2z with z∈Ω, i.e. Ω+Ω=2Ω for convex Ω. It then treats the Euclidean norm |x+y| as if it were Lebesgue measure. Dilation by 2 multiplies volume by 2^d, so |Ω+Ω|=2^d|Ω|. For the unit disc in R^2 this gives 4|Ω|, not 2|Ω|. The claimed factor 2^{1/p}|Ω|^{1/p} is false for d≥2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2^{1/p}|Ω|^{1/p} by 2^{d/p}|Ω|^{1/p} (since Ω+Ω=2Ω), and propagate this to the dependent convex statements. The non-convex bound stays valid.
issues.overall_effect: The convex-domain 'simplified bounds' in Proposition prop:supported_approximation_sobolev_space_local, Corollary cor:Barron and the introduction use a wrong constant. The correct constant is exponential in d.
issues.title: Convex-domain improvement |Ω+Ω| ≤ 2|Ω| is false (should be 2^d|Ω|)
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and short, but the advertised factor 2 becomes a dimension-dependent 2^d, which changes the stated simplified bounds in dependent results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: M^2_{v_s}(\rr d) = L^2_s(\rr d)\cap \cF L^2_s(\rr d)= Q^s(\rr d)

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:approximation_sobolev_space_local needs the norm of M^2_{v_{s1}⊗v_{s2}} (product weight ⟨x⟩^{s1}⟨ξ⟩^{s2}). Lemma lem:shubin identifies M^2_{v_s}, with v_s=⟨(x,ξ)⟩^s on R^{2d}, with Q^s and L^2_s∩FL^2_s with one common s. The product weight is not dominated by ⟨z⟩^{s2}; it is only dominated by ⟨z⟩^{s1+s2}. So ||f||_{M^2_{v_{s1}⊗v_{s2}}} is not bounded by ||f||_{Q^{s2}}, nor by ||f||_{L^2_{s1}}+||f||_{FL^2_{s2}}, which controls only a sum of weights, not the product. The 'if and only if' in the proof is also not given by Theorem thm:embeddings, which supplies only sufficiency.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound with Q^{s1+s2} (or L^2_{s1+s2}∩FL^2_{s1+s2}) via the weight inequality ⟨x⟩^{s1}⟨ξ⟩^{s2}≤⟨z⟩^{s1+s2}, and drop 'if and only if'.
issues.overall_effect: Both bounds in eq:Hilbert_approximation_bound_L are unsupported as stated, and so is the 'uncertainty principle' interpretation.
issues.title: Shubin/L2-weighted corollary uses mismatched weights
issues.why_classification: The result survives only in a weakened form with stronger smoothness/decay assumptions, which needs a contained reformulation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f\in M^{p,q}_{1\otimes v_{s_2}}(\rr d)$, with $0<p<\infty$, $0<q\leq 2\leq r$,

issues.failure_explanation: The embedding lemma bounds ||χ_Ω f||_{M^{p,q}} by ||χ_Ω f||_{FL^q}, not by ||f||_{FL^q}. For s_2≥n+1 the indicator χ_Ω destroys decay of the Fourier transform, so ||χ_Ω f||_{FL^q_{v_{s2}}} can be infinite while ||f||_{FL^q_{v_{s2}}} is finite. Theorem thm:approximation_sobolev_space_local is stated for f in M^{p,q}_{v_{s1}⊗v_{s2}} on all of R^d, with s_1>d/p' when p>1. The proposition assumes only f∈M^{p,q}_{1⊗v_{s2}}, so the theorem is not applicable. The factor |Ω+Ω| is also written without the exponent 1/p of the lemma. The lemma's own proof also uses Young's inequality L^q*L^1 for q<1, which fails, and drops the weight in the window's Fourier norm.

failure_location.quote: The proof is a combination of \cref{thm:approximation_sobolev_space_local} and \cref{cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space} as well as \cref{cor:FourierLebesgue_embedding_in_modulation_space_convex}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the theorem to ψf with a smooth cutoff ψ≡1 on Ω, use boundedness of multiplication by ψ on weighted FL^q (restricting to q≥1 or treating q<1 separately), and restate the constants with their dependence on ψ/Ω. Add the x-weight hypothesis for p>1.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bound in terms of the global FL^q_{v_s} (Barron) norm, with constant |Ω+Ω| (or 2|Ω|), is not established. Corollary cor:Barron inherits this gap.
issues.title: Fourier-Lebesgue local approximation: bound for χ_Ω f is applied to f, and weight s_1 is ignored
issues.why_classification: A contained localisation argument and a changed constant are needed, but the method and the N^{-1/2} rate survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The inversion formula represents f as an integral over all (y,η)∈R^{2d} (and b∈R). The measure μ_f has density V_φf(y,η) on that whole set. The dictionary D̃_Ω contains only atoms with y∈Ω, so μ_f is not a measure on D̃_Ω and ∫ρ dμ_f over D̃_Ω does not equal f. Contributions from y∉Ω are simply dropped. The restriction y∈Ω is used only to get uniform boundedness of sup_y||v_u ∂^γφ(·−y)||_∞. For general f∈M^{p,q}_m, with mass far from Ω, the claimed rate N^{-1/2}||f||_M with atoms localised near the bounded set Ω is therefore not justified. The variation-norm bound ||f||_{K(D̃_Ω)}≤C||f||_M is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: which in turn allows us to represent $f$ in the integral form containing all the required components:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum one must either allow y∈R^d and control sup_y norms with a y-dependent weight absorbed into the x-weight s_1, or give a separate argument that atoms with y in a bounded set can reproduce f.
issues.overall_effect: The global approximation theorem, its Feichtinger-algebra and potential-Sobolev corollaries, and the introduction's claim of a global bound with bounded y-set are unproved and possibly false.
issues.title: Global theorem: dictionary restricted to y∈Ω cannot reproduce f as claimed
issues.why_classification: The advertised feature (a dictionary with spatial shifts in a fixed bounded set) fails with the given representation, so the proof architecture and dictionary must change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While our theoretical framework assumes $\sigma \in W^{k, \infty}(\rr{})$.
providing empirical support for the efficiency suggested by our theoretical bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: ReLU is unbounded and not in W^{1,∞}(R), so it is outside the theorems' hypotheses. The proposed justification (ramps/teeth as sums of ReLUs) does not give atoms of the dictionary form. The windows φ(a−t) have a fixed centre t, while a shifted ramp term (a−b_i)_+φ(a−t) would need a bias-dependent t. The ramp is only W^{1,∞}, so n≥2 is not covered. The experiments therefore test an architecture not covered by the theorems, and the 1/√N, dimension-free, and 'consistent with theoretical estimates' statements are not backed by the formal results.

failure_location.quote: We employ the standard ReLU activation in our numerical experiments.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the experimental claims as heuristic and not covered by the theorems, or use a bounded W^{k,∞} activation with the exact dictionary form in the experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The statements that the experiments validate or are consistent with the theory, and the remarks about the N^{-1/2} baseline, are unsupported.
issues.title: Experiments with ReLU claimed to be covered by, and supportive of, the theory
issues.why_classification: A rewording or a change of experimental activation suffices; no theorem is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it would vanish on a non-empty open set, and hence on the entire real plane

issues.failure_explanation: The triangle inequality gives |V|≥|T_2|−|T_1|, a bound below T_2, not the claimed |V|>T_2. At (0,0) one has |V|=1/(2π)=T_2 (Lemma lem:relu-origin), so the strict inequality fails. The identity-theorem step is invalid: a real analytic function with an isolated zero does not vanish on an open set. Zeros of a complex-valued STFT for ω≠0 are generically isolated, and the claim V_φσ(x,0)>0 for all x is not proved. 'Never vanishes' is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the statement by: V_φσ is continuous with V_φσ(0,0)=1/(2π), so (t,τ) with τ≠0 and V≠0 exist (Condition (A)). Drop the strict bound and global non-vanishing.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's claim and lower bound are wrong or unproved. Only the weaker Condition (A) is actually needed by the theorems, and it follows from continuity and V(0,0)=1/(2π).
issues.title: Non-vanishing of the STFT of ReLU: strict lower bound false and zero-set argument invalid
issues.why_classification: Everything used downstream follows from a short continuity argument; only the corollary's overstated content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The 'classical' estimate |erfc(z)|≤C e^{-|z|^2}/(1+|z|) for all z∈C is false: erfc(z)→2 as Re z→−∞, and |erfc(ib)|~e^{b^2}/(b√π). Consequently |T_1|≤C(1+|x|+|ω|)e^{-π(x²+ω²)} fails. At x=0, |T_1|→1/(2π). The stated bound also fails for x→+∞, ω=0: V_φσ(x,0)=∫t_+e^{-π(t−x)^2}dt grows like x, whereas the bound decays like e^{-πx²}. Hence σ=t_+ is not in M^{1,∞}_{v_s⊗1} for every s (it is only in M^∞).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the claim, or replace it with the correct bound |V_φσ(x,ω)|≲(1+|x|) (growth in x) and the membership σ∈M^{∞} only.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix decay corollary and the remark that the framework applies to ReLU via modulation-space membership are false. They are not used in the main proofs.
issues.title: False complex erfc estimate gives false decay bound and false modulation-space membership of ReLU
issues.why_classification: The corollary and remark are false and need a corrected statement and proof. The main theorems do not depend on them, so the loss is contained.
